report:
**Conclusion: The claim is false.** Drinking boiled garlic water does not cure COVID-19.

**Evidence:**

- **No scientific proof exists.** Health professionals told AFP Fact Check as early as February 2020 that there is no evidence garlic is an effective COVID-19 treatment. The claim that boiled garlic cures COVID-19 emerged early in the pandemic and has been repeatedly debunked.
- **WHO explicitly addresses the myth.** The World Health Organization's "COVID-19 Mythbusters" page states there is currently no licensed medication to cure COVID-19 and addresses garlic-related misinformation directly. WHO podcast "Science in 5" Episode #8 also busts myths about garlic and COVID-19.
- **FactCheck.org confirmed garlic is not a cure.** In February 2020, FactCheck.org listed boiled garlic among online posts claiming "cures" for the new coronavirus, classifying it as benign but false.
- **General antiviral properties ≠ COVID-19 cure.** While one review in PMC notes garlic possesses antiviral activity and organosulfur compounds with potential prophylactic use against viral infections generally, no solid evidence confirms garlic directly prevents or cures COVID-19 specifically. Scientific consensus remains inconclusive regarding its direct impact on COVID-19.
- **Snopes and The Packer** also flagged the web-fueled claim that garlic has power over coronavirus as false.

The claim is classified as **False** by multiple fact-checking organizations and health authorities.

**Sources:**
- https://factcheck.afp.com/theres-no-scientific-proof-tonic-onions-ginger-garlic-and-lemon-can-cure-covid-19
- https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters
- https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7434784/
